correctness.rationale: The period map is M(d) κD^{-1} M(d)D and the exact independent symbolic Laurent-polynomial computation proves det(I-κ^{-1}P)=-d^3(1-d) Σ_{pairs}((u-v)^2/(uv)). Strict negativity at every interior d for nonconstant positive diagonal data makes the monic characteristic polynomial negative at λ=1, hence an eigenvalue and Perron radius above 1. Both endpoints and the homogeneous case have Perron radius exactly 1 by cycle-weight product and stochasticity. The 2-site boundary follows via diagonal similarity to a symmetric kernel and convexity of a Euclidean matrix norm, with triangular degeneracies bounded at no migration. All 448 exact rational cases corroborate but do not replace the universal algebraic proof.

value.rationale: The old directed-cycle example establishes possibility but does not settle robustness over heterogeneous patch profiles or migration rates. This theorem completely classifies all reciprocal-fitness profiles for the minimal three-patch nonreversible movement cycle and proves every nontrivial partial rate has a strict linear-growth advantage, while the equal-profile and endpoint regimes are sharp. This structurally distinguishes genuine directed cycle effects from two-patch exchange. The claim is intentionally confined to deterministic linear population dynamics and does not assert nonlinear persistence or empirical outcomes.
